How to effectively report problems

If you’re experiencing a problem on our site, we recommend first searching our Help Center using the search bar at the top. If you can’t find your answer, we recommend posting your question on our User Community, where both IMDb users and IMDb Staff can help answer your questions.

We recommend the following to ensure your problem is understood and promptly addressed:

  1. Be very specific/detailed:
    Explain exactly what you were doing when the problem occurred and what happened. If you received an error message on your screen, please copy and paste it in your message. If you can, post a screenshot or provide a step-by-step description of what happened. Providing these details will help us understand and help solve your problem.

  2. Include the URL:
    Always cut and paste the URL to the exact page of the site where you experienced the problem. Even if it seems redundant, the site has literally millions of pages, so including the link can help us pinpoint the problem.

  3. Check for similar reports:
    The reason why we encourage users to check the support community is not just because there might already be an answer to your question, but also because there might be similar reports from other users. When the same problem is shared by a large number of users, it’s definitely more likely to be caused by something else which we can investigate and prioritize a fix.

  4. Try correcting the error:
    If the problem you noticed is with information rather than performance of a site feature, you can submit an update for our processing team to review. Information on IMDb can be updated directly via the “Edit Page” button located at the bottom of almost every page on the site which contains data. If you have noticed information that is inaccurate or out of date or in need of any kind of revision, the best and fastest way to fix is to make the change yourself, instead of simply reporting it, by clicking on the “Edit” button and submitting an update. If you need help getting started, our Contributor Zone section has plenty of useful information and guides.

  5. Try another browser/computer:
    Some problems may be caused by incompatibilities with specific browsers or other software, or network issues limited to the user’s location or connection. If possible, try accessing the same feature with a different browser (i.e. if you are using Firefox try Chrome). If you can, try reproducing on a different computer or device. If the issue goes away, this means that the problem was with your browser or device.

How to report security issues and vulnerabilities

IMDb welcomes reports from security researchers and experts about possible security vulnerabilities.

If you believe you have found a security vulnerability on IMDb.com, please review the information here and submit the details of your findings through the web form, including your findings and detailed instructions regarding how to reproduce the issue.

Following the link above, please access the web form under Report a security vulnerability on Amazon Retail services or products. Once in the web form, choose Amazon Subsidiaries in the “Asset” field, and proceed through the steps in the form to report a security issue for IMDb.

Be advised, IMDb does not currently participate in a bug bounty program.

IMDb is an Amazon company, and handles security issues using Amazon’s processes.

How to report suspicious emails

If you receive an email claiming to be from IMDb that seems suspicious, it may be a phishing email. A phishing email appears to be from a reputable source, but in reality it is sent from an outside party attempting to access your personal information by getting you to open an attachment containing malware or click on a link that redirects to a potentially dangerous website.

Some phishing emails may even contain a link to a website that looks like IMDb.com, but is not a legitimate site. The website may ask for your IMDb username and password or try to install unwanted software on your computer. If you receive a message like this, you should delete it without opening any attachments or clicking any links.

If you wish to report a suspicious email claiming to be from IMDb that you believe is a forgery, please forward phishing emails and other suspected forgeries directly to stop-spoofing@imdb.com.

IMDb Partners

ERC | Famous Frames | MPA | MPTV | WGA | WireImage

ERC

Since 1974 Exhibitor Relations, Co. has supplied studios, networks and media outlets with the verifiable knowledge and insight necessary to maintain a distinct advantage in a rapidly changing and increasingly competitive marketplace. Exhibitor Relations provides essential services to the film industry and news media and anyone interested in movies and box office data.

With state-of-the-art research tools, ERC continues to expand and revolutionize the research process for entertainment industry clients and other global businesses. For further information, please visit Exhibitor Relations.

Famous Frames

Since established in 1988, Famous Frames has held its position as the preeminent talent agency representing artists that specialize in storyboards, shooting boards, comp art, illustration and full-service cinematic production

Famous Frames represents a roster of 100+ of the world’s top illustrators. For more information, please visit Famous Frames.

MPA

The Motion Picture Association (MPA) provides IMDb with ratings reasons, which helps describe the content of movies listed on IMDb. For more information, please visit MPA.

MPTV

The Motion Picture and Television Archive (MPTV) is dedicated to the preservation, documentation, and promotion of the most outstanding past and present photography from all facets of the entertainment industry. MPTV’s growing library includes over one million fully documented images by more than fifty photographers; many never before published with biographies of the photographers wherever available. For more information, please visit MPTV.

WGA

The Writers Guild of America (WGA) has a well-defined process for determining credits on projects produced under its jurisdiction. These productions are generally USA-controlled live-action film and TV projects, produced either by studios or major independent producers. In 1999, the WGA began furnishing credits directly to IMDb. The absence of the WGA indicator on earlier credits should not be construed as a sign of unofficial status, merely a sign of age.

In general, the credits determination process works as follows: When the film is finished shooting, the producer sends a notice to the guild and the writers proposing the writing credits. If any writer disagrees with those credits, or if the proposed credits require mandatory arbitration (i.e., a producer or director sharing a writing credit), a WGA arbitration committee reads all drafts of the script and various supporting materials and determines the actual/official credits. If there is no source material (novel, play, article, etc.) and the same writers receive credit for both the story and screenplay, the credit is “written by”. The “story by” credit is used when the basic narrative structure was originally written with intent to be used for a movie (as opposed to a short story) and the actual screenplay had different authors. A shared “story by” credit is the minimum awarded to the author of an original screenplay. If there was previously existing source material but the writer creates a substantially new and different story from the source, then the “screen story” (or “television story”) credit is used. Finally, the “screenplay by” (or “teleplay by”) credit is used to denote the screenplay (teleplay) authorship if the story credit had to be separated as above. In rare cases, “adaptation by” can be awarded to a writer who shapes the script without qualifying for one of the above credits. There are other specialized credits used for television programs such as documentaries and audience participation shows. Within each of these categories, members of a writing team are joined by “&”; teams or writers working on separate drafts are joined by “and”.

IMDb will not accept uncredited writers for titles with WGA-determined credits. For more information, please visit WGA.

WireImage

WireImage provides high-quality, event-based imagery and related services to traditional publishing, new media, broadcasting, and other commercial enterprises worldwide. Their imagery is captured by an elite team of professional photographers using state-of-the-art digital imaging equipment and delivered to customers via the Internet, FTP, or physical shipment.

WireImage has extensive experience covering major entertainment, fashion, professional sports, news, corporate, and feature events. Their team comprises acclaimed photographers and industry veterans whose work is featured in major domestic and international publications. They bring decades of experience in producing and licensing professional imagery to thousands of corporate buyers worldwide.

WireImage also has an archive of over two million images that represent one of the premier collections covering the American entertainment and music history over the past 30 years. This archive at WireImage is expanding daily and comprises contemporary entertainment, documentaries, features, sports, and other event-based imagery from around the world. For more information please visit WireImage.

IMDb Single Sign-On with Amazon

Updated 15-July-2026

This article explains how IMDb and IMDbPro customers are signed in with their existing Amazon account, to get recommendations tailored to your taste, track titles on your Watchlist, rate what you watch, and also contribute to the world’s most popular entertainment database. This experience offers consistency and simplicity, with the same sign-in and account across IMDb, IMDbPro and Amazon using your existing Amazon account.

IMDb is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Amazon and was acquired in 1998.

What’s new

Eligible Amazon customers will be automatically signed into IMDb.com with a newly created IMDb account, unless you already sign into IMDb with Amazon. For more information see our guide.

You will see one of the two experiences below:

  1. You are signed in as [name] from Amazon. Not you? Learn more | Sign out
  2. You are signed in as [name] from Amazon. Not you?** Sign in another way**
Frequently asked questions
Who is eligible for this new experience?

Currently only US customers using IMDb.com on a web or mobile Chrome, Firefox, or Safari browser will see this new experience.

Who isn’t eligible for this new experience?

  • Customers with Amazon accounts registered in Japan or China.

    • For more information, see our Japan and China guides.

  • Customers with Amazon Teen accounts.

What happens if I select “Sign out”?

You will be signed out of this newly linked IMDb account, and the account will be requested for deletion. If you selected this option and want to keep this newly linked account, just create a new IMDb account with your Amazon credentials!

What happens if I select “Sign in another way”?

You will be signed out of this newly linked IMDb account, and the account will be requested for deletion. You will then be taken to the IMDb login page. If you selected this option and want to keep this newly linked account, just create a new IMDb account with your Amazon credentials!

How do I unlink my accounts?

If you already have an IMDb account linked with your Amazon account, you will need to go the Delete account page in your Account Settings. You will need to be logged in to an IMDb account to do this.

Please ensure that you’re deleting the correct IMDb account before proceeding.

You will see a link to your IMDb profile, the number of titles in your Watchlist, how many titles you’ve rated, the number of titles you’ve reviewed and your profile badges. If this profile data matches your IMDb account previously linked with your Amazon account, you may need to check which email address is associated with the account before opting to unlink and delete your newly created IMDb account.

If you have any issues signing in to your IMDb account, please contact us.

IMDb Support Community access - You’re about to leave IMDb.com

You’re about to leave IMDb.com and access the official IMDb Support Community, where you will be able to get answers from customer service and other IMDb members, who are encouraged to help each other to get the most out of our site. Often the community provides answers and solutions faster than our staff can respond directly.

If prompted to login or signup, please do not use your IMDb or IMDbPro account information. The IMDb Support Community is hosted on an external third party website (Sprinklr). You can post in the community by creating a new account on the third party website (you’ll only need to do this once).

Notes:

  • The IMDb Community is a public forum. Anything you post will be visible to everyone. For issues regarding accounts/billing issues, please contact our support staff privately using the form below.

IMDb Text Formatting

IMDb Markdown Guide

These formatting tags (“markdown”) are supported on IMDb profiles, lists, polls, and bios.

  • Tag: ; Usage: ; Appearance:
  • Tag: [b]…[/b]; Usage: Make [b]some text[/b] bold; Appearance: Make some text bold
  • Tag: [i]…[/i]; Usage: Make [i]some text[/i] italic; Appearance: Make some text italic
  • Tag: [u]…[/u]; Usage: Underline [u]some text[/u]; Appearance: Underline some text
  • Tag: [link=title#]; Usage: Create IMDb title/person links:; Appearance: Create title/person links:
  • Tag: [link=person#]; Usage: [link=tt0076759]; Appearance: Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope (1977)
  • Usage: [link=nm0000182]; Appearance: Jennifer Lopez
  • Tag: [link=title#]…[/link]; Usage: Create IMDb title/person links with custom text:; Appearance: Create IMDb title/person links with custom text:
  • Tag: [link=person#]…[/link]; Usage: [link=tt0076759]Star Wars[/link]; Appearance: Star Wars
  • Usage: [link=nm0000182]J.Lo[/link]; Appearance: J.Lo
  • Tag: [link=…]…[/link]; Usage: Create an IMDb hyperlink with custom text:; Appearance: Create an IMDb hyperlink with custom text:
  • Usage: [url=https://www.imdb.com/trailers/]Trailers[/url]; Appearance: Trailers
  • Tag: [quote]…[/quote] *; Usage: Block quote:; Appearance: Block quote:
  • Usage: [quote]If you build it, he will come.[/quote]
  • Appearance: > If you build it, he will come.
  • Tag: [spoiler]…[/spoiler] *; Usage: Spoilers: [spoiler]The character dies at the end.[/spoiler]; Appearance: Spoilers: The character dies at the end.
  • Tag: - (hyphen); Usage: Create an unordered list:; Appearance: Create an unordered list:
  • Usage: - The Godfather
  • Usage: - The Dark Knight; Appearance: - The Godfather
  • Usage: - Mad Max: Fury Road; Appearance: - The Dark Knight
  • Usage: [i]Note: Always start a new line.[/i]; Appearance: - Mad Max: Fury Road
  • Appearance: *Note: Always start a new line.
  • Appearance:
  • Appearance: *

* The [quote] and [spoiler] tags have a different appearance on iOS and Android apps.

Is my IMDb Profile page private?

Data and lists that you’ve marked as private will not be displayed. While logged into your IMDb account, you’ll still be able to view this information on your “Your Profile” page. To quickly view what’s been marked as private, we recommend viewing your IMDb Profile page while logged out of IMDb.

Badges you’ve earned by rating or contributing to IMDb will show on your IMDb Profile page. There isn’t a way to hide these from public view at this time.

All IMDb accounts will automatically have a profile page. There isn’t a way to remove your profile page, except to delete your entire IMDb account - rather than deleting your account, we recommend marking your profile activity such as; ratings, lists, check-ins, etc., as private.

Manage Your Email Subscriptions and Watchlist Notifications

We provide a number of ways to keep you updated on the entertainment world through IMDb Informational Emails and IMDb Subscription Emails and Newsletters which are found in Email Preferences.

IMDb Informational Emails include editorially curated updates ranging from what’s new and trending to tips and tricks to get the most out of your IMDb experience. IMDb Subscription Emails and Newsletters contain personalized updates based on your selection(s).

If you have shows or movies in Your Watchlist, but have not received email notifications, there are few things to check:

  1. Go to Email Preferences and sign-in if prompted.

    • Subscription emails are only sent to users that have been active on the site within the last two years. If you have not visited a page while logged into your IMDb account within the last two years, this may resolve the issue.

  3. Under IMDb Subscription Emails and Newsletters, check that you’ve selected Watchlisted Shows on Tonight (for shows) and/or Watchlisted Movies in Wide Release (for movies).

    • Make sure Do not send me informational emails is not checked (under IMDb Informational Emails).

  5. Go to Change your Details and make sure your Country / Region of Residence is selected as we’ll match your selection to the release details for movies and shows on your Watchlist.

    • Movies receiving a wide release (300+ cinemas) with a release date in the next seven days are supported in the following countries: Argentina, Austria, Australia, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Germany, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Ireland, India, Italy, Mexico, New Zealand, Portugal, and United States.
    • We have TV release details for shows in over 100 countries, including those listed above for movies, and send Watchlisted Shows on Tonight updates for shows airing on the same date as the email.
    • IMDb only stores release information for the date of first release, so particularly for TV-shows, notifications will only be sent for the date of first broadcast. Re-runs are not supported.

Note: If you intend to add a series to Your Watchlist, but only add a single episode, you won’t receive Watchlist emails for episodes other than the one you’ve added. You’ll need to go to the series and add it to Your Watchlist.

Press information

  • See IMDb’s Press Room


Please note: IMDb’s press email alias is for use exclusively by journalists on deadline. Inquiries about other topics will not receive a response. For all other inquiries, please contact IMDb’s customer service team.

Sign in with Facebook not available

As of October 6, 2022, you will no longer be able to use “Sign in with Facebook” to access your IMDb account. If you previously logged in with Facebook and are having difficulty accessing your account, all you need to do is update your IMDb password using the reset password process to regain access. Once you have done this, you will be able to use the ”Sign in with IMDb“ option for any future logins.

If you previously used “Sign in with Facebook” to access your IMDb account, and are having trouble accessing it currently, please take the following steps to retain access to your account:

    1. Go to Reset Password Page.
    2. Input the email associated with your Facebook account and select “Continue”. You will receive an email with a link to reset your IMDb password.
    3. Return to the IMDb sign in page and select “Sign in with IMDb” to log in to IMDb with your email and new password.

If you have previously followed these instructions or have already set a password for your IMDb account, please return to the sign in page and use the “Sign in with IMDb” login method.

If you do not reset your password, you will not be able to access your IMDb account and the associated data (e.g. contributions, lists, ratings, recommendations, etc.).

For details on other IMDb account issues, please visit our help page: IMDb login/registration issues

Frequently Asked Questions

I no longer have access to the email I used to sign in with Facebook. How can I reset my password?

Please contact Customer Service for help to recover your account.

I completed the reset password process but my data, lists, and ratings are gone. How can I recover my data?

It is possible the account you updated your password for was registered to a different email address than your Facebook account. Please contact Customer Service for help to recover your account/data.

Sign-in issues

Updated 24-September-2025

Can’t sign in to IMDb?

Below are a few common fixes, plus important cases to review.

Quick fixes:

  • Go to the Sign-in page, and try again.
  • If you’ve forgotten your password, use Password assistance to reset it.
  • Your password must be at least 8 characters and include numbers and letters. The characters <>,‘ are not supported.

Still stuck? Select your situation

If the above quick fixes did not help, the issue usually falls into one of the below cases. Choose the one that matches what you’re seeing, and attempt to resolve the problem with the specific instructions.

Case 1 - You now use your Amazon account to sign in.

Issue: Your IMDb email and password credentials have stopped working.

Why: Your IMDb account is now accessed with your Amazon credentials (email address/mobile number and password). Your ratings, Watchlist, reviews, contributions, lists, and all other IMDb data are still there.

What to do:

  1. Select Sign in with Amazon on the Sign-in page.
  2. Use your Amazon email/mobile number and password (the ones you use on Amazon.com).
  3. Complete any Two-Step Verification prompts if necessary.

Tips

  • If you have multiple Amazon accounts, try the one that matches your previous IMDb email.
  • If you have trouble accessing your Amazon account, visit Amazon’s account issues page.

Other common issues

  • “We cannot find an account with that email address”: If you don’t recall creating an IMDb account before, you can create a new account with Amazon. You can also first try signing in with a different email address you might have used on IMDb.
  • “You already have an IMDb account”: The email address you’re trying to create an account with already belongs to an IMDb account. Please sign in with that email address instead of creating an account with it.

Need more help?

If you need help accessing your account, please visit the Contact Us page, and include the email address registered to your account and any further details on the sign-in issue you’re experiencing.

Site Preferences

As an IMDb user, you can configure the following site settings on the Site Preferences page.

Title display country/region - allows our registered users to choose the title displayed based on the country of their choice e.g. ‘France’. This preference will allow our users to have all the titles they view on www.imdb.com displayed as it was when released in France.

As part of the “Title display country” preference - our registered also users have the option to choose ‘Original’ title display. The Original title in the Country of Origin - which prior to the previous changes was the default on www.imdb.com.

Examples: As always, it is easier to explain this functionality with an example. Using this title.

With your “Title display country” set to ‘Original’ - you will see the Title Text as ‘Ronde de nuit’. This was the title of this French film when it was first released in France.

With your “Title display country” set to ‘US’ - you will see the Title Text as ‘Night Patrol’ - which was the title name for the US release.

With your “Title display country” set to ‘Poland’ you will see the Title Text as ‘Nocny patrol’ - which was the title for release in Poland.

Title display language - This option is for use for countries that have more than one language – therefore allowing our registered users to choose which of the languages for that country they want displayed.

Examples: Using this title.

With your “Title display country” set to ‘Canada’ – and the “Title display language” set to ‘English’ – you will see the Title Text as ‘Bethune’.

With your “Title display country” set to ‘Canada’ – and the “Title display language” set to ‘French’ – you will see the Title Text as ‘Bethune, héros de notre temps’

Default Title Display: For users that are not logged into www.imdb.com, and as the default for our registered users who have not selected a preference - we will display the localized version of the title they are looking for based on their geo-location. Users in France will see the title as released in France.

Contributors: Show reference view with full cast and crew - This is an advanced, data-centric view built for our top contributors and is not recommended for general use, as it is deliberately missing many IMDb features.

Trouble Signing in to IMDb (Browser is Redirecting on Device)

Updated 20-October-2025

If you’re having trouble signing in to IMDb - especially on Samsung devices - you may notice your browser switching during sign-in (for example, from Chrome to Samsung Internet). This can cause your sign-in to restart or appear unsuccessful.

Why this happens

Some devices automatically use their default browser to complete secure sign-in. This can cause your sign-in attempt to restart if you begin the process in a different browser.

How to fix it

To sign in successfully:

  • Complete sign-in in the browser that opened automatically (It’s your device’s default browser).
  • Or change your default browser to the one you prefer (such as Chrome or Firefox) and then try again.
  • Or use the IMDb app (iOS or Android), which will keep your sign-in consistent.

Still having trouble?

If you’ve followed these steps, and still can’t sign in, please use the Contact Us form, and provide your device model and which browsers were involved in the issue (e.g., Chrome → Samsung Internet).

Use of Amazon accounts registered in China on IMDb

Updated 13-October-2025

If your Amazon account is registered in China and linked to an existing IMDb or IMDbPro account, here is how to now sign in to IMDb. However, if you are in China and creating a new account on IMDb or IMDbPro, you will need to do so with an Amazon account not registered in China.

At a glance for customers in China

  • Amazon accounts registered in China can no longer use “Sign in with Amazon” or “Login with Amazon” to access existing IMDb accounts.
  • Your IMDb data (e.g., ratings, Watchlist, reviews, lists, contributions, history, etc.) is not affected.
  • Existing customers: Sign in using IMDb email and password. You can reset your IMDb password if you’ve forgotten it.
  • New IMDb customers: To create a new IMDb account in China, you must have an existing account or create an Amazon.com account (Amazon site), not a local Amazon account for China.

Existing IMDb and IMDbPro customers in China — what to do now

If you previously signed in — via “Sign in with Amazon” — with your Amazon account registered in China, you must now use “Sign in with IMDb”.

Steps
  1. On the IMDb sign-in page, select “Sign in with IMDb”.
  2. Enter your IMDb email and password.
  3. Don’t know your IMDb password? Select Password assistance, enter the email on your IMDb account, and set a new password.

Good to know:

  • Your IMDb account ratings, reviews, lists, Watchlist, and history remain unaffected on your account.
  • After you sign in with IMDb, you can keep using IMDb with your IMDb email and password.

New to IMDb or IMDbPro in China

To register a new account on IMDb, you can use an Amazon.com account (not a local Amazon China account).

Steps:
  1. Go to Amazon.com and select Create account.
  2. Verify your email or phone number and finish setup.
  3. Return to IMDb and “Sign in with Amazon” (use your Amazon.com sign-in credentials).

Messages you may see in China

  • “We cannot find an account with that email address”: This displays during “Sign in with Amazon” when it previously did not. If you’re in China, this likely means you have an Amazon account registered in China. You can instead select “Sign in with IMDb” to sign in. If you forgot your password, you can select Password assistance to reset your IMDb password.
  • “You already have an IMDb account”: The email you’re trying to create an account with already belongs to an IMDb account. Sign in with that email instead of creating an account for it.

IMDbPro members in China

Your IMDbPro membership and profile continue as usual. Sign in using the method above that applies to your account — IMDb email/password for an existing IMDb account, or an Amazon.com account if you are creating a new IMDb account. You can continue to update IMDbPro billing details where you manage your IMDbPro membership today.

Need more help?

If you need help accessing your account, please visit the Contact Us page, and include the email address registered to your account and further details related to the login issue you’re experiencing.

Use your Amazon account for IMDb

Updated 22-July-2026

Your Amazon account is now your login to IMDb. Here’s how to get started depending on how you currently sign in. Already using “Sign in with Amazon” to access IMDb. You’re all set. Keep signing in the same way!

IMDb is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Amazon, and was acquired in 1998.

Contents

  • What’s changing?
  • Why did we make this update?
  • Find your IMDb experience (quick links)
  • Troubleshooting / FAQs
  • What happens after I migrate my account to Amazon?
  • What happens if I don’t migrate?
  • Migrate via IMDb Account Settings
  • Related help (quick links)

What’s changing?

  • IMDb now uses Amazon’s account system for sign-in and new account creation. If you sign in with alternative methods, you will be prompted to migrate your account to sign in with Amazon going forward.
What stays the same?
  • Existing IMDb accounts remain active. If you choose not to migrate, you can continue signing in with your IMDb email and password. We’ll remind you to migrate and sign in to IMDb with your Amazon credentials every 60 days.
  • Your IMDb data stays with you Your ratings, Watchlist, reviews, and contribution history all remain on your account.

Why did we make this update?

  • Consistency: The same sign-in and account across Amazon and IMDb.
  • Simplicity: Fewer credentials to manage; use your existing Amazon account for a more seamless experience.
  • Personalization: Better recommendations tailored to your taste.

Find your IMDb experience (select the option that best describes how you use IMDb)

  • I sign in on the IMDb desktop site →
  • I sign in on the IMDb mobile site →
  • I sign in on the IMDb iOS app →
  • I sign in on the IMDb Android app →
  • I sign in with Google or Apple →
  • I’m new to IMDb →

Troubleshooting / Frequently Asked Questions

You couldn’t find an IMDb account with my email address!

If you try to sign in to IMDb with Apple or Google after you’ve migrated your account to Amazon, you may see a “There was a problem” error when trying to sign in to IMDb. Your IMDb account is now managed with your Amazon credentials. Use these to sign in to IMDb by selecting Continue with Amazon.

My Amazon account is already in use!

If you see the below screen when trying to migrate your IMDb account to Amazon, continue with your IMDb account and try migrating with a different Amazon email address. This can be done from your IMDb Account Settings.

I’m not sure which sign-in method I used!

Try your most recent sign-in method first. If that doesn’t work, try another option on the sign-in page.

My email changed on Amazon, how do I sign in?

If you changed your email on Amazon, your IMDb sign-in updates on its own. Sign in with your updated Amazon credentials.

My email changed on IMDb (before I tried to migrate), how do I migrate my account?

If you changed your IMDb email before migrating your account to Amazon, use your most recent IMDb email and password to start, and follow the steps from your preferred IMDb experience below (e.g. desktop, mobile site, iOS, Android, Google/Apple).

Do I need to create a new account?

No, you’ll need to sign in to your existing IMDb account to migrate. This way you won’t lose any user data or contribution history on your IMDb account. Follow the steps from your preferred IMDb experience below to sign in (e.g. desktop, mobile site, iOS, Android, Google/Apple).

What happens after I migrate my account to Amazon?

All of your IMDb data stays with you, but now you have the seamless experience of the same sign-in credentials and account across Amazon and IMDb. Just make sure to use your Amazon credentials when signing in to IMDb going forward!

You will now manage your account email, mobile number, and password (with Two-Step Verification) via the Amazon account settings page: Amazon.com > Account & Lists > Account > Login & security.

⚠️ Important

Deleting your Amazon account also deletes your IMDb and IMDbPro account, and all associated data. This includes any active IMDbPro membership.

What happens if I don’t migrate?

If you decline migration to Amazon, you can continue to sign in with your IMDb credentials, but you’ll be prompted again after 60 days to migrate.

What if I continue not signed in?

If you use IMDb without signing in, you will miss out on features such as; ratings, your Watchlist, reviews, and more!

I keep getting stuck in a loop!

If you can sign in to IMDb, go to your Account Settings and try to migrate to Amazon from there. Check out our instructions below for more details.

I sign in on the IMDb desktop site

You may be asked to migrate your IMDb account to sign in with your Amazon account.

Here’s what to expect:

  1. Sign in with your IMDb email and password.

  2. You’ll see a message:

    1. Since IMDb is an Amazon company, you can sign in with your Amazon account for a more seamless experience. Your Watchlist, ratings, and reviews will stay the same.

  4. Confirm your IMDb account, then sign in to Amazon to complete migration.

    1. If you don’t have an Amazon account, you can create one from the sign-in page.

  6. You’re all set. From now on, use your Amazon account to sign in to IMDb.

If you choose not to migrate your IMDb account, you will be prompted to do so after 60 days.

If you select Not now here, you can always migrate your IMDb account to Amazon from your Account Settings.

I sign in on the IMDb mobile site

If you use the IMDb mobile site, your experience will be the same as the desktop web steps above to migrate your account.

  1. Sign in to your existing IMDb account.
  2. Select Sign in with IMDb.
  3. Enter your IMDb account credentials.
  4. Migrate your account to Amazon? Next: Sign in to Amazon.
  5. Use your Amazon account email and password.
  6. You’re all set. From now on, use Sign in with Amazon.

If you see that your Amazon account is already in use with another IMDb account, you’ll have to continue with the IMDb account you’ve just signed in with. If you still want to migrate, try a different Amazon email address. You can do this from your IMDb Account Settings. If you’re still experiencing issues migrating, or you can’t sign in to IMDb to access your Account Settings, please Contact Us.

I sign in on the IMDb iOS app

These steps are the same as on IMDb desktop, but styled for the IMDb iOS app.

  1. On your IMDb iOS app, Sign in to your existing IMDb account.
  2. Select Sign in with IMDb.
  3. Enter your IMDb account credentials.
  4. Migrate your account to Amazon? Next: Sign in to Amazon.
  5. Use your Amazon account email and password.
  6. You’re all set. From now on, use Sign in with Amazon.

If you see that your Amazon account is already in use with another IMDb account, you’ll have to continue with the IMDb account you’ve just signed in with. If you still want to migrate, try a different Amazon email address. You can do this from your IMDb Account Settings. If you’re still experiencing issues migrating, or you can’t sign in to IMDb to access your Account Settings, please Contact Us.

I sign in on the IMDb Android app

The steps are the same as on IMDb desktop, but style for the IMDb Android app.

  1. On your IMDb Android app, Sign in to your existing IMDb account.
  2. Select Sign in with IMDb.
  3. Enter your IMDb account credentials.
  4. Migrate your account to Amazon? Next: Sign in to Amazon.
  5. Use your Amazon account email and password.
  6. You’re all set. From now on, use Sign in with Amazon.

If you see that your Amazon account is already in use with another IMDb account, you’ll have to continue with the IMDb account you’ve just signed in with. If you still want to migrate, try a different Amazon email address. You can do this from your IMDb Account Settings. If you’re still experiencing issues migrating, or you can’t sign in to IMDb to access your Account Settings, please Contact Us.

I sign in with Google or Apple

If you sign in to IMDb with Google or Apple, we recommend migrating your account to sign in with Amazon. The steps to complete migration can be seen and are listed below.

(Example screenshots are for the Apple experience, these steps will be the same for Google linked IMDb accounts)

If your IMDb account is linked to Google or Apple:

  1. Select Sign in with Google or Apple (whichever you normally use to sign into IMDb)
  2. Enter your Google or Apple credentials.
  3. We’ll ask you to sign in to IMDb with your Amazon account.
  4. Sign in with your Google or Apple details to confirm it’s you.
  5. Then sign in to (or create) an Amazon account to link your IMDb account and data.
  6. You’re all set. From now on, use Sign in with Amazon.
I’m new to IMDb

If you’re new to IMDb and an Amazon account already matches the email you’re using to create an account, you’ll be asked to sign in to IMDb with your existing Amazon account. There’s no need to create a new Amazon account.

If you’re not actually new to IMDb, and already have an account, the next screen will let you know and ask you to sign in before migrating your IMDb account to Amazon.

If you’re new to Amazon, use the grey “Create an account” button in the above center screenshot, and create an account. Going forward, use those details to sign in to IMDb.

Migrate via IMDb Account Settings

You can always migrate your IMDb account to Amazon via your Account Settings. Check out the screenshots below for steps.

If you’re still experiencing issues migrating, or you can’t sign in to IMDb to access your Account Settings, please Contact Us.

  1. If you’re signed in with Amazon on IMDb, manage your account email, mobile number, and password (with Two-Step Verification) by visiting the Amazon account settings page: Amazon.com > Account & Lists > Account > Login & security.
  2. If you’re signed in with IMDb, manage your account email/password by visiting the IMDb Account Settings page.

⚠️ Important

Deleting your Amazon account also deletes your IMDb and IMDbPro account, and all associated data. This includes any active IMDbPro membership.

About IMDb & Amazon

IMDb is an Amazon company and was acquired in 1998.

User naming - Username, Real name, IMDb page

This article provides information into the difference between Username, Real name, IMDb name page and Contribution details.

Quick links - Username | Real Name | Contribution | IMDb Name Page

Username

Everyone with an IMDb account has a username - it’s a label associated with your user activity if you’ve made that content public. This includes:

  • User reviews
  • Lists
  • Your Watchlist
  • Ratings
  • Polls
  • Check-Ins

Your username also appears on Your Profile and provides you with a consistent way to be represented across IMDb.

You can change your username by visiting the “Edit profile” page in the Account Settings section.

You can also update your IMDb Profile’s bio to personalize your profile page further.

Both your IMDb username and profile bio can also be edited on the IMDb mobile apps (iOS & Android), and the IMDb mobile site.

Real Name

Everyone with an IMDb account also has a private contact name (real name). This appears only in your view, in the navigation bar in the upper right of every IMDb page. Your real name is used for communication with customer service and e-mails you receive from IMDb.

Contributions

Your username is used internally to identify your contributions to IMDb. Contributions are always anonymous with these exceptions:

  • You can, if you choose to, include a ‘by’ line on mini-bios and plot summaries submitted through the main submission interface (clicking “Edit page” on title and name pages on www.imdb.com or pro.imdb.com)
  • For plots summaries submitted via mobile, you can choose between “Anonymous”, ”Real name”, or “Username”

IMDb name pages

If you are an entertainment industry professional with credits listed on IMDb, you may have an IMDb name page. This is different than your username.

See also: What’s the difference between an IMDb page and user profile?

What is an Enhanced Page?

Certain pages on IMDb are what we call ‘Enhanced Pages’. These are specially designed pages showcasing certain new titles or popular people found on IMDb. You will only see them on some titles and in some countries, and usually just for a limited time. After this period of time, these previously Enhanced Pages will return to a normal IMDb page appearance.

Enhanced pages often include moving backgrounds, sound, and video features. Exactly what enhanced elements you see in your browser may depend upon your location, your browser settings and the browser add-ons. Some enhanced title pages may not appear in certain countries, or on specific devices.

All assets on Enhanced Pages are created and approved by IMDb in an advertising partnership. Enhanced Pages are not available upon request.

What is IMDb?

Launched online in 1990 and a subsidiary of Amazon.com since 1998, IMDb is the world’s most popular and authoritative source for movie, TV and celebrity content, designed to help fans explore the world of movies and shows and decide what to watch.

Our searchable database includes millions of movies, TV and entertainment programs and cast and crew members.

IMDb can help you:

    • Jog your memory about a movie, show, or person on the tip of your tongue
    • Find the best movie or show to watch next
    • Empower you to share your entertainment knowledge and opinions with the world’s largest community of fans

For fans deciding what to watch and where to watch it, we offer local movie showtimes, ticketing, trailers, critic and user reviews, personalized recommendations, photo galleries, entertainment news, quotes, trivia, box-office data, editorial feature sections and a universal Watchlist. To learn more about watching Trailers, Clips, Featurettes, and IMDb Originals, please see the IMDb Video FAQs.

IMDb creates new original video content each week and you can find it all at IMDb Originals.

You can find new videos highlighted every day on the IMDb homepage via your desktop computer or IMDb app.

You can read more about IMDb in our Press Room.

To create your IMDb account, please go to the Registration page.

To learn more about our services for entertainment industry professionals, please visit What is IMDbPro?

What is the difference between IMDb and IMDbPro?


IMDb is the most authoritative source of entertainment information, with features designed to help fans explore the world of movies and shows and decide what to watch.

  • Get answers – Jog your memory about a movie, show, or person on the tip of your tongue or binge on information about the movies and shows you love.

  • Watch wisely – Find the best movie or show to watch next, making the most of your screen time.

  • Share your passion – Share your entertainment knowledge and opinions with the world’s largest community of fans.

IMDbPro includes all the data from IMDb plus features specifically designed for entertainment industry professionals, including the world’s biggest stars, the most influential decision-makers, and the leading entertainment companies and brands.

  • Showcase your talent –manage your IMDb profile by adding images and videos; plus, highlight your bio, credits, and portfolio.

  • Get connected – access contact and representation details, client rosters, and shared connections from our comprehensive database.

  • Stay informed – view project listings, box office performance, IMDb data trends, shared credits and daily industry news.

  • Discover new opportunities – search in-development projects, build customized lists, browse casting notices, and apply to roles with your claimed IMDb Page.

What software are you using to run IMDb?

The Software

IMDb began as a set of scripts and data files which had to be run on a UNIX system. These scripts still work and are available to download on the IMDb Datasets page. When WWW was invented we created a website in Perl which allowed anyone with a browser to access our database without having to know how to download and install anything. We do not distribute this software.

Our entire website and nearly all of our internal-use tools are created with open source software such as Apache, and the usual collection of GNU and Linux utilities. The software that runs the database itself was completely developed in-house.

Note: For security reasons we will not disclose any additional information.

The Hardware

We run Linux on Intel-based hardware.

Again, for security reasons we will not disclose any additional information.

Database Statistics

If you would like a detailed breakdown of IMDb statistics, please visit the Press Room page. We do not disclose website traffic figures to the public, however you can see that Alexa rates us as one of the top 100 websites.

Running Your Own Copy of IMDb

IMDb stays true to its Internet roots and core principles, thus we make available files and software to construct part of the database on your own system (for private, non-commercial use only). For more information on how to do this and the supported operating systems, please visit our IMDb Datasets page.

Commercial use

If you’re looking for information on licensing IMDb content for commercial use, please see the Content Licensing page.

What’s the difference between an IMDb page and user profile?

Updated 8-April-2026

This article covers the following topics:

  • What is an IMDb account?
  • What is an IMDb name page?
  • Using a user account to claim a name page

What is an IMDb account?

A user account is associated with your IMDb login for every registered e-mail address.

It’s connected to your general activity across IMDb.com - giving you the ability to interact with:

  • User ratings
  • User lists
  • Badges
  • Contributions

The “Your Profile” page *(e.g. https://www.imdb.com/user/p.colneedham{style=“background-color: #fefefe;” target=“_blank” rel=“noopener”})* lets you see a history of the these features, and more!

As seen above, Ratings Insights are now featured on IMDb profiles. Ratings Insights visualize your ratings behavior over time, showing you how your ratings distribute across the IMDb 1 to 10-star rating scale, various Interest categories, and the release years of the movies and TV shows you’ve rated. This is always visible to you even when you set your ratings to private. This feature is also visible when you visit other user’s profiles (as long as their ratings are set to public) to see how their tastes line up with your own.

You can easily navigate to your IMDb profile page from anywhere on the site, by clicking on your name in the top right corner of the site navigation bar, and clicking “Your Profile”.

There are now three different color rating stars that indicate various types of IMDb title ratings on a review or profile:

  • Yellow - The IMDb overall community rating
  • Blue - Your IMDb user rating
  • Green - Another user’s IMDb rating (i.e. the user whose review/profile you are viewing)

If you are viewing your own review page, a green star will not appear.

See image below for an example of the three different ratings on an IMDb profile.

{margin-right:10px;=“” <=“” p=““}

What is an IMDb name page?

An IMDb name page (e.g. https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0350453{style=“background-color: #fefefe; color: #ff5522; text-decoration-line: underline; outline: 0px; cursor: pointer;”}) displays information relating to a person’s industry portfolio, such as:

  • Filmography
  • Biography
  • Trivia
  • News


This information is added by user accounts via the “Edit page” button. These submissions are reviewed by the IMDb team.

Using a user account to claim a name page

To claim a name page with an IMDbPro membership, you must have a user account - then follow our instructions on how to claim your page (you can create a new name page if you don’t already have one) and these are then linked together.

What’s your phone number?

We don’t offer phone support, as our Customer Service is carried out through our online support channels.

If you can’t find the answer to your question on this Help site, please visit the Contact Us page and select your issue from the option list, followed by “Email” - a member of the support team should get back to you within 24 hours.

Please make sure to include as much supporting information in your request as possible to help us provide the answer.

Where does the information on IMDb come from?

In short, the information in IMDb comes from various sources!

While we actively gather information from and verify items with studios and filmmakers, the bulk of our information is submitted by people in the industry and visitors like you!

In addition to using as many sources as we can, our data goes through consistency checks to ensure it’s as accurate and reliable as possible. However, there’s absolutely no substitute for an international team of entertainment fans with an encyclopedic knowledge of trivia and a large assortment of reference works (and we include in this group many of our loyal contributors).

Our sources of information include, but are not limited to:

  • on-screen credits
  • press kits
  • official bios
  • autobiographies
  • interviews

Given the sheer volume and the nature of the information we list, occasional mistakes are inevitable and, when spotted/reported, they are promptly verified and fixed. That’s why we welcome corrections and submissions. Our service is provided for the information of users only.

Accordingly, IMDb shall under no circumstances be liable for any loss or damage, including but not limited to loss of profits, goodwill or indirect or consequential loss arising out of any use of or inaccuracies in the information. All warranties express or implied are excluded to the fullest extent permissible by law. Please see our terms of use/copyright information for further details.

Why do I need to enable my cookies on IMDb?

IMDb uses cookies to identify registered users. A cookie is simply a piece of text that is saved in your browser’s configuration to allow our servers to recognize you every time you visit IMDb. In order to access your IMDb account, you will will need to enable cookies on your browser.

If your browser is configured to reject cookies, you can still access and search IMDb but you will not be able to use any of the personalized features reserved to registered users. To make sure cookies are enabled, please check your browser configuration (usually under the Security or Advanced Configuration section).

Why do I need to enter a Captcha?

You might see a CAPTCHA when you sign in, create an account, or our systems spot activity that could be automated.

The CAPTCHA may be distorted text to type or an image-based puzzle (e.g., “select the motorbikes” or “solve this puzzle”). If it is difficult to read or solve, click the arrow icon and receive a new CAPTCHA.

CAPTCHAs prevent bots that create fake accounts or overload IMDb servers, helping keep the site fast, accurate, and secure for all customers.

Why should I register on IMDb?

Updated 24-September-2025

Registering on IMDb opens up the ability to enjoy the following features:

    • Get personalized recommendations and discover new movies and shows you’ll love.
    • Create your Watchlist to track everything you want to watch and get notified when movies open in theaters.
    • Rate all the movies and shows you’ve seen to improve your recommendations.
    • Share a review of your favorite movies and shows with the world’s largest community of entertainment fans.
    • Contribute data to IMDb that will be seen by millions of people and get cool badges.
    • Create and share lists of titles, names, images & videos.
    • Vote in thousands of Polls.
    • Personalize your IMDb experience, including title language and local ratings certificates.
    • Check-in to titles as you watch them.

You can easily create an IMDb account by selecting “Create an account” on the Sign-in page.

To learn more about our services for entertainment industry professionals, please visit: What is IMDbPro?

You have so much information! Where should I start?

The menu bar located at the top of every page at IMDb has links to our main site features. All our pages also include a search box to quickly locate any movie, TV show or person.

  • We also have a very comprehensive index with an alphabetical list of the most popular features available. If you are not sure of what you are looking for, you can also browse titles by Genre/Interest or Keyword.

  • If you are looking for specific titles or people and need more powerful search functions, you should use our advanced search feature (on desktop site). For example, you can search for titles by specific genre, country, language, or year; you can also search for title by Instant Watch Options (IMDb TV or Prime Video) or search for people by specific gender or star sign.

IMDbPro: Industry Contacts

How do I add a new company to IMDbPro?

You can add a new company page a couple of ways:

  1. Connecting a new company to a title page (For example, if your company has a credit on a title, you can add your company via the title’s page)
  2. Connecting a new company to a name page. (If your company has an employee or client currently listed on the site, you can edit that person’s page and add a new company)

The easiest way to create a new company on IMDbPro is to attach it to a piece of information already on the site.


Not a member yet?

Adding your new company via a Title page.

  1. To attach a new company to an existing title page we will need to start there. For example your company is a new Product Placement company and just signed a contract to provide product placement services for a new James Bond movie. Start by going to the title/movie on IMDbPro, and clicking Edit Page at the top.

  2. In the overlay panel contribution form, select the Company Credits section. Currently, there are 4 specific types of companies as well as “Miscellaneous Company” listed in this section. Please choose to Add 1 credit (or more if you need) to the appropriate section. Note: All companies that are not Production Companies, Distributors, Sales Reps or Special Effects companies fall into the Miscellaneous Companies bucket (such as the product placement company in this example).



  3. On the next page, you will type in your company’s name and include the country code in square brackets. Let’s call the company Hollywood Products. Since it is based in the United States, it will have [us] listed at the end like this: Hollywood Products [us].
  4. Suggestions will be shown as we do not want to create duplicated companies and if a suggestion shown matches your company name please only select this if you are sure it is the correct page otherwise you will add a new credit to another company.

  5. Please refer to our Company Naming Conventions submission guide.

  6. And also the full list of country codes we use.

  7. If you chose Miscellaneous Company, you will now choose a role describing what your credit is for. Or you can type in the role (such as Vehicles).
  8. Click Check these updates.

  9. On the next page, you’ll see either green, yellow or red boxes.

  10. If you see green boxes, it means your company is already in the database and you can follow the remainder of the on-screen instructions.

  11. If you see red boxes, there is a problem with your submission. Most likely you’ve not added the country code in square brackets (see above and feel free to copy the brackets in our example if you don’t know what they are).

  12. If you see yellow boxes, there are additional questions for you to answer. Most often, you will see a list of potential matches for your company name. If you see a match, please choose it if you are confident the page is correct. If you don’t see a match, the last option on the list is: “Add this as a new company” with the additional option of adding contact data to the company. Please choose that option if applicable.
  13. Click Re-check these updates.

  14. You should now see green boxes, meaning the data is ready to submit. If you see yellow boxes, please read the questions on the screen and clarify/verify what it needs. Click Re-check these updates.

  15. At this point, all the boxes should be green and you can click Submit these updates.

  16. Once you submit the change, you will be taken to a Thank You screen which will have your Contribution Number listed for future reference. This reference number will also be sent to your email address and will always be available in your Contribution History.

Adding your new company via a Name page.

  1. To attach a new company to a person, you will need to start at their name page. For example, the individual is the CEO of your company.

  2. Go to the person’s page on IMDbPro, and go to the Contacts tab. Select Add contact details.** **

  3. Select which type of Contact Details you’d like to add, and then click Continue.

  4. On the next page, you will type in your company’s name and include the country code in square brackets. Let’s call the company Hollywood Products. Since it is based in the United States, it will have [us] listed at the end like this: Hollywood Products [us] .
  5. See our Company Naming Conventions submission guide

  6. See the full list of country codes we use.

  7. Add in the Job Title. You can also add any appropriate Job Type from the drop-down or contact details.
  8. Click Check these updates.

  9. On the next page, you’ll see either green, yellow or red boxes.

  10. If you see green boxes, it means your company is already in the database and you can follow the remainder of the on-screen instructions.

  11. If you see red boxes, there is a problem with your submission. Most likely you’ve not added the country code in square brackets (see above, you are welcome to copy the brackets in our example if you don’t know what they are).

  12. If you see yellow boxes, there are additional questions for you to answer. Most often, you will see a list of potential matches for your company name. If you see a match, please choose it. If you don’t see a match, the last option on the list is: “Add this as a new company”. Please choose that option.

  13. Click Re-check these updates.

  14. You should now see green boxes, meaning the data is ready to submit. If you see yellow boxes, please read the questions on the screen and clarify/verify what it needs. Click Re-check these updates.

  15. At this point, all the boxes should be green and you can click Submit these updates.

Once you submit the change, you will be taken to a Thank You screen which will have your Contribution Number listed for future reference. This reference number will also be sent to your email address and will always be available in your Contribution History.

How do I add contact information for an individual or company?

Only IMDbPro members can view and update contact information. Contact information on IMDbPro is representation information (what talent agent represents an individual), employer details (the company where someone works), and contact information for companies in the entertainment industry.

While logged into your IMDbPro membership, you can add or update contact details for your IMDb page from the “Contacts” tab or by clicking the ”Edit” button in the Contacts section on the right of your IMDbPro name page’s Overview:

Where do I find contact information for an individual or company?

All contact information we have for a given individual or company is available on that person’s or company’s IMDbPro page.

Access to the information referenced below requires an IMDbPro Premium Subscription while members with an IMDbPro Basic Subscription may have limited access. Learn more on the IMDbPro Subscription comparison page.

A Person’s Contact Information

For example, let’s look at Natalie Portman’s page. On this page, you’ll find her employer and her reps (Talent Agents, Managers, Publicists, Legal reps, etc.) listed in the right column, or in the Contacts tab.

A Company’s Contact Information

For example, the United Talent Agency (UTA) page. On this page, you’ll find office locations (“Branches”), staff, clients and filmography credits as well as other details.

Branch: Branch locations, along with other details will be listed in the Contacts section on the right.

Staff: You will see a partial list of staff in the middle with a link to view the entire staff roster on its own page. To see the full staff roster, click the Staff header, which will take you to the Staff page. You can sort that page by name, title, STARmeter or branch to more easily find individuals.

Clients: You will see a partial list of clients below the staff box with a link to view the entire clients list on its own page.

To see the full client list, click the Clients header, which will take you to the Clients page. The client list is sorted by STARmeter with each of the reps listed next to each client. If you are having trouble locating someone on the list, try using your browser’s Find function by clicking Ctrl + F and typing their name.

    • : To access Discover Titles, click any of the options under the “Titles” dropdown in the nav bar at the top of the page.
    • :
    • : You can also access Discover Titles directly through this link: https://pro.imdb.com/discover/title/.
    • : #### Can I access IMDbPro Discover on the mobile site and apps?
    • : No, Discover People and Discover Titles are currently not available on the mobile site and apps.
    • : #### Can I access IMDbPro Discover on all browsers?
    • : Yes, but we recommend using Chrome, Firefox, or Safari for the best experience.
    • : #### What “Keywords” can I use?
    • : Keywords provide you with the ability to search for any text or content within IMDb. Based on your specific needs, you can use any keywords. For example:
    • : - Keywords in IMDb bio - searches within a person’s biography. You can search for “Where did the person grow up?” with keywords like “Los Angeles”, or “What was their breakthrough?” like “Severance”.
    • : - Job title keywords - searches within a person’s job title. Examples are CEO, CFO, CMO, Partner, President, etc.
    • : - Plot keywords - searches within all plot keywords associated with a title. Examples are Polynesia, husband-wife relationship, air-to-surface missile, ancient civilization, bar fight, blockbuster, etc.
    • : - Role/Credit keywords - searches within a person’s credit. Examples are choreographer, intimacy coordinator, craft services, dog handler, etc.
    • : - Filming location keywords lets you find titles that filmed in specific places. You can search for cities like “Barcelona” or “Cape Town,” countries like “Japan” or “New Zealand,” or even points of interest like “The Louvre” or “Mojave Desert.”
    • :
    • : #### How can I save my filter selections?
    • :
    • : Once you have selected your desired filters, click on the Save filters button below the filter options. To save your specific filter set, confirm the “Filter name”, and click Save.
    • : To access your saved filters, you can click on the Your saved filters link at the top of the search filter options.
    • : #### How can I clear my filter selections?
    • :
    • : While on IMDbPro Discover, there are two places where you can clear your filter selections. You can locate the Clear all filters link at the top of the page (just above the results display), or also the Clear all filters button below the filter options (left panel).
    • : #### How is the “Relevance” sort determined?
    • : “Relevance” uses multiple data points such as profession, popularity, top professions associated with a person, and many more to provide you with the best results.
    • : #### How can I reorder items in my list?
    • : Go to Your lists and select the list you would like to update. Click on “Manage”, select “Reorder list” from the drop-down, and you will be able to manually reorder your list by numerical order.
    • : Note: By default, your list is sorted by last added.
    • : #### Can I use more than one instance of Discover at a time? (e.g., two windows with different parameters/filters/lists)
    • : Yes, you most certainly can! You are welcome to use multiple instances of Discover simultaneously.
    • : #### Can I use IMDbPro Discover to search for Companies?
    • : Not at this moment.
    • : #### Can my default view when visiting IMDbPro Discover be a saved filter and/or default list?
    • : Not at this moment.
    • : #### How do I submit feedback or report bugs?
    • : Please contact us to send your feedback.

  • What do the “Professional experience” search options do?

  • The Professional experience search options help you find people based on their credited profession and professional affiliations:
    • Onscreen talent, filmmakers, and crew based on their profession, role (credited role), and number of credits released in a year range.
    • Executives and assistants based on their profession and job title.
    • Reps (agents, managers, legal, and publicists) based on their profession and client count.
    • Professional affiliations to find individuals based on guild, union, or association eligibility.


  • To get started, you can select a profession, and based on that profession, you will get refined filters. For example:
    • Actor - You will find the option to filter by minimum number of released credits and release year range.
    • Director - You will find the option to filter by role/credit the director had in the title, minimum number of released credits, and release year range.
    • Executive - You will find the option to search people based on job titles such as CEO, Head of TV, etc.
    • Talent Agent - You will see the option to find people based on how many clients they have.

  • What do the “Credit details” search options do?


  • The Credit details search options help you find people based on their released titles.
  • The filter options include:
    • Title type (movie, TV, etc.); - Production budget
    • Genre (Action, Adventure, etc.); - Box office performance (US and Canada)
    • Plot keywords; - Company credits (companies that were involved in the titles)
  • The Discover algorithm uses the year range and number of credits you specified in the “Professional experience” search option to determine the year range and number of titles to match with your selection in the credit details search option.
  • For example, if you selected Actor with minimum five credits between 2015 to 2020 and a budget of >50MM, the selection will include people who have at least five credits released between 2015 and 2020 in which they were actor and at least five credits released between 2015 and 2020 with a budget of >50MM.

  • What do the “Personal details” search options do?


  • The Personal details search option exposes filters such as:
    • Age-playing range
    • Birthplace
    • Biography
    • Physical attributes
    • Employment details
    • Skills
    • Gender / Gender Identity
    • Race, Ethnicity, & Nationality
    • Disabilities
    • Sexual orientation
    • and more
  • This allows you to narrow your search to create a custom list of individuals based on their profiles.
  • The self-verified asterisk in the Personal Details section refers to information that has been added by entertainment industry professionals to their claimed IMDbPro page.

  • What does the “Company details” search option do?


  • The Company details search options are available for professions such as:
    • Executives
    • Assistant
    • Talent Agent
    • Manager
    • Legal
    • Publicist
  • It helps you find people who are employed in the companies you chose.

  • What do the “Representation” search options do?


  • The Representation search options help you find people who have specific type of reps and/or if they don’t have specific type of reps.

  • What does the “Collaborations” search option do?

  • The Collaborations search option finds people who all worked on multiple projects (up to 3). It can help you find people who frequently collaborate or have shared experience on the same kinds of projects.

  • What does the “Name search” search option do?


  • The Name search search option allows you to find people by text associated with a name. (e.g., Audrey)

  • What does the “Media” search option do?


  • The Media search option allows filtering for people with media such as:
    • Headshots (i.e., primary image)
    • Featured images
    • Demo reel

  • What do the “Awards & film festivals” search options do?


  • The Awards & film festivals search options allows filtering for people based on whether they were recognized at an event, including Awards Ceremonies and Film Festivals.
  • Filter types include:
    • Wins Only/Wins and Nominations
    • Awards/Film Festival/Event Name
    • Minimum number of wins or nominations
    • Specific year range

  • How can I see more information about a person in the Discover People card?



  • Selecting the Discover People card (or clicking in the empty space in a card) will enlarge the card, providing additional details such as representation/clients, featured images, demo reels, awards, and more — all in one convenient view.

  • Why is the Discover People card different for different professions?

  • The Discover People card is designed to provide you with the most contextual information for a person based on the profession you selected.

  • Can I find deceased people using Discover People?

  • Discover People does not include the profiles of deceased people by default, but you can include them by selecting “Include deceased” within the “Personal details” search options.

  • Can I find adult actors and actress in the Discover People?

  • Discover People does not include the profiles of adult actors and actresses.

  • How can I add people from the Discover People card to a List?


  • You can add one person to your active list by clicking on the Add to list button on the card.

  • You can also add one or more people at a time by selecting the checkbox next to the person and then using the bulk add to list (blue button) feature at the top of the Discover People page just above the results display.

  • How can I improve my discoverability in the Discover People tool?

  • You can improve discoverability by keeping your profile up to date.
  • We recommend to make sure you add all your credits (including Role), Representation information, Images (Primary and featured images), Known For, Demo reel videos, Company information, awards and film festivals, etc.

What’s New in IMDbPro Lists?

    • New and improved IMDbPro Lists interface: - New Grid View for IMDbPro Lists; - Added functionality to copy and/or move items from one list to another list: - You can now sort lists based on individual columns
    • New and improved IMDbPro Lists interface: - Shared lists link now active for 30 days; - Added functionality to copy and/or move items from one list to another list: - You can search for lists, by name or description
    • New and improved IMDbPro Lists interface: - Added functionality to export your IMDbPro list to a CSV file; - Added functionality to copy and/or move items from one list to another list: - You can search people/titles in lists, by name or notes

What are lists on IMDbPro, and how are they different from lists on IMDb?

Lists can be created by any IMDbPro member for people or titles. Lists are designed to make your job easier, whether you are looking to fill a role, build your network, share ideas, or conduct industry research. You can find Your Lists under “Your Tools” in the navigation bar on IMDbPro.

Lists created on IMDbPro are separate from lists created on IMDb, and cannot be migrated from one site to the other. IMDbPro lists can ONLY be created for titles or people (image and video lists cannot be created on IMDbPro). IMDbPro lists cannot be made publicly discoverable like lists on IMDb; however, you can share a list from IMDbPro with other people (even those without an active IMDbPro membership).

What are IMDbPro Industry Lists?

IMDbPro Industry Lists is a feature that provides list of people and titles across various criteria in the entertainment industry. These lists are powered by IMDbPro data and IMDbPro’s industry partners. Industry lists can be found on the IMDbPro homepage or directly accessible via: https://pro.imdb.com/list/new/industry

How do I create a list?

There are a few different ways to create a list on IMDbPro:

  • From the Your Lists page (desktop): to create a people list, navigate to the “People” tab. To create a title list, navigate to the “Titles” tab. Once on the desired tab, click on the Create list button. You will then be prompted to enter the list title in the “List name” field, and an optional list description. Once you have input these details, select “Create”

    – –



  • From the Your Lists page (mobile/app): select “Create a list” in the upper-right corner of the page

    – –


  • From a name/title page (desktop): select “Add to list”, then select “+ Create list”




  • From a name/title page (app): select “Add to list”, then select “Create new list”
    – –


  • From Discover (desktop): select “Create a list”, then select “Create”


How can I edit my list?

To edit the name or description of your list:

  • From the desktop website: while viewing the list, tap on the title or description to edit; OR when viewing the “Your lists” page, select the 3 dots on the right-hand side of the list, then select “Edit”

    – –

  • From the app: select “Edit list” at the top of the list; OR select the 3 dots in the upper-right corner of the list, then select “Edit list”

How can I add items to my list?

To add an item to your list, navigate to a name or title page, select “Add to list”, then select the name of the list (on the app, you will need to select “Done” after selecting the name of the list).


Via Discover (only on IMDbPro website)


How can I delete items from my list?

To delete an item from your list:

  • From the desktop website: select the 3 dots to the right of the name/title in your list, select “Delete”, then select “Delete” on the pop-up confirmation box – –

  • From the app: select the 3 dots to the right of the name/title in your list, select “Remove from list”, then select “Yes. Delete!”

    – – –

How can I move/rearrange the order of list items?

For “People” lists, you can sort your list by Name, STARmeter, Talent Agency, or Management.
For “Title” lists, you can sort your list by Name, Title type, Run time, MOVIEmeter, IMDb Rating, or Production Co.

To reorder your IMDbPro list on the desktop website, click on “Manage” in the upper-right corner of the list, then select “Reorder list”. IMDbPro lists cannot be reordered via the IMDbPro app or mobile website at this time.

How can I delete my list?

Once a list has been deleted, it can can not be restored. To delete your list:

  • From the desktop website:** select t he 3 dots to the right of the list, select “Delete list”, then select “Delete” in the pop-up confirmation box
    \


  • From the app: select the 3 dots in the upper-right corner of the list, select “Delete list”, then select “Yes. Delete!” – – –

How can I share my list?

To share your IMDbPro list, select the “Share” option in the upper-right corner of the list page on the desktop website, then choose whether you’d like to copy the shared link or trigger your device’s default email program to compose an email. IMDbPro lists cannot be shared via the IMDbPro app or mobile website at this time.

How can I export my list?

You can export your list by selecting the “Export” option found in the upper-right corner of your list.

How can I print my list?

You can print your list by using your browser’s Print function.

Is there a limited number of lists I can create?

Yes, each IMDb user is limited to 999 lists.

Is there a limit to the size of my list?

Yes, lists can not extend beyond 10,000 titles.
